investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Failing: Kubernetes Cluster Exhausted of kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-08-01T12:36–12:43Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 6-node Kubernetes cluster had zero available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots (2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm; 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector), and preemption could not free capacity. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never reached a running state.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that matched the pod's node affinity/selector had exhausted their kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource quota, and the remaining 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector constraints at all. Because the pod remained unscheduled for 134–145 seconds (exceeding the eval's implicit readiness window), the probe timed out before any VM was provisioned, leaving all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) empty and causing the contract assertion failures. This is a Kubernetes infrastructure capacity/scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents swarm backend in the production-api environment; no evidence of a user-traffic or broader service outage is present in the packet.

investigation.summary: The eval for the published-observability-snapshot check failed because the snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json is 695 minutes old, which exceeds the contract's maximum allowed age of 300 minutes. This is an isolated eval failure scoped to the snapshot freshness assertion; all three sibling public-website checks passed, and no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence.
investigation.rootCause: The GitHub Actions workflow responsible for regenerating and publishing the observability snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json has not run successfully within the required 300-minute window. The snapshot is 695 minutes old at the time of the eval run (2026-08-01T12:43:38Z), meaning the last successful publish occurred approximately 11.6 hours prior. The contract asserts snapshotAgeMinutes must be <= 300 (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 482); the observed value of 695 directly violates this assertion. The root cause is a missed or failed GitHub Actions workflow execution, not a problem with the public website itself or the eval runner infrastructure.

possibleCauses: Most likely: The scheduled GitHub Actions workflow that generates and publishes the observability snapshot did not execute or did not complete successfully within the last 300 minutes, leaving the previously published file in place.

Second: The GitHub Actions workflow ran but failed mid-execution (e.g., a job step error, permissions issue, or Pages deployment failure) before writing a new snapshot, so the stale file was not replaced.
Third: GitHub Actions was experiencing a platform-level delay or queue backlog that prevented the scheduled workflow from starting on time, resulting in a gap exceeding 300 minutes.

Fourth: The workflow schedule itself was modified, disabled, or the triggering cron expression was changed such that the run interval now exceeds 300 minutes — though no suspect changes in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges support this hypothesis and it remains unconfirmed.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Creation Failing: Kubernetes Cluster Exhausted of kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-08-01T12:36–12:43Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 6-node Kubernetes cluster had zero available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots (2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm; 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector), and preemption could not free capacity. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never reached a running state.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that matched the pod's node affinity/selector had exhausted their kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource quota, and the remaining 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector constraints at all. Because the pod remained unscheduled for 134–145 seconds (exceeding the eval's implicit readiness window), the probe timed out before any VM was provisioned, leaving all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) empty and causing the contract assertion failures. This is a Kubernetes infrastructure capacity/scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents swarm backend in the production-api environment; no evidence of a user-traffic or broader service outage is present in the packet.

investigations.title: Remote Agent State Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigations.summary: The remote-agent-state eval failed because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed with the same or near-identical scheduling error, and no required evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was collected because the agent pod never became schedulable within the eval timeout window.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote agent swarm has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. With 0 of 6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote agent pod submitted during this eval run was stuck Unschedulable for ~134–145 seconds before the eval timed out. Because the agent pod never started, the runner in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (line 1905, createAgent call) never returned an agent identity, and the contract-required evidence fields orgId, agentId, readyState, and state were never written. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote agent VM scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 affinity-matching nodes: the scheduler message explicitly states 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on those nodes, and preemption found no victims, indicating all VM slots are occupied by running workloads with no lower-priority pods to evict.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: only 2 of 6 nodes are eligible for remote agent pods; if those 2 nodes are at capacity there is zero scheduling headroom regardless of overall cluster size.

TERTIARY — Transient cluster capacity spike: a burst of concurrent remote agent workloads (from users or other eval runs) may have consumed all kata.peerpods.io/vm slots simultaneously, causing a temporary but complete scheduling blackout.

LOWER CONFIDENCE — Cluster node count or VM resource quota has not been scaled to match demand growth: the fixed pool of 2 eligible nodes with a finite kata.peerpods.io/vm quota may be structurally undersized for current load.

investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agents feature exhausted its schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity across all 6 nodes at the time of the eval run. With 2 nodes reporting "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" and 4 nodes failing pod affinity/selector matching, no node could accept the remote agent VM pod. The pod remained Unschedulable for 134–145 seconds across all three checks before the eval timed out. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure, not an application code defect. No evidence of a user-facing production incident or real traffic impact is present in the supplied packet; this is an eval-layer failure reflecting the state of the cluster at the time the observability probes ran.

The ~5-minute window across all three checks (12:38–12:43Z) is consistent with a transient burst.

investigations.title: published-observability-snapshot Eval Failure: Stale GitHub Actions Snapshot (snapshotAgeMinutes 695 > 300)
investigations.summary: The eval for the published-observability-snapshot check failed because the snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json is 695 minutes old, which exceeds the contract's maximum allowed age of 300 minutes. This is an isolated eval failure scoped to the snapshot freshness assertion; all three sibling public-website checks passed, and no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence.
investigations.rootCause: The GitHub Actions workflow responsible for regenerating and publishing the observability snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json has not run successfully within the required 300-minute window. The snapshot is 695 minutes old at the time of the eval run (2026-08-01T12:43:38Z), meaning the last successful publish occurred approximately 11.6 hours prior. The contract asserts snapshotAgeMinutes must be <= 300 (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 482); the observed value of 695 directly violates this assertion. The root cause is a missed or failed GitHub Actions workflow execution, not a problem with the public website itself or the eval runner infrastructure.
proof: failed-check.message: 'snapshotAgeMinutes expected <= 300 but got 695' — the single violated assertion is the freshness bound (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 482: { "path": "snapshotAgeMinutes", "max": 300 }).

failed-check.evidence: snapshotAgeMinutes=695, source='github-actions', hasLiveSource=true, generatedAtPresent=true — the snapshot exists and was produced by GitHub Actions but is stale by 395 minutes.
expected-output.contract: maxAgeMinutes=300 is both the contract assertion and the value returned in the snapshot itself, confirming the freshness SLA is 300 minutes.

source.infra/evals/status/features.json:383: check is registered as required=false, statusImpact='informational', staleAfterMinutes=360 — the registry staleAfterMinutes (360) is looser than the contract assertion (300), but the binding eval assertion is the contract's max:300.
sibling.public-observability-page, sibling.public-models-page, sibling.public-marketing-pages: all three sibling checks passed with HTTP 200 responses, ruling out a broad website or CDN outage.
failed-check.evidence: overall='major_outage' in the stale snapshot payload — this reflects the status recorded when the snapshot was last generated, not a live system state at eval time.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:2168-2173: the runner fetches the snapshot via publicJsonUrl(args.publishedSnapshotUrl) and passes it through statusSnapshotEvidence(), confirming the eval reads the live published file and the age is computed from the file's own timestamp.
possibleCauses: Most likely: The scheduled GitHub Actions workflow that generates and publishes the observability snapshot did not execute or did not complete successfully within the last 300 minutes, leaving the previously published file in place.

Second: The GitHub Actions workflow ran but failed mid-execution (e.g., a job step error, permissions issue, or Pages deployment failure) before writing a new snapshot, so the stale file was not replaced.
Third: GitHub Actions was experiencing a platform-level delay or queue backlog that prevented the scheduled workflow from starting on time, resulting in a gap exceeding 300 minutes.

Fourth: The workflow schedule itself was modified, disabled, or the triggering cron expression was changed such that the run interval now exceeds 300 minutes — though no suspect changes in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges support this hypothesis and it remains unconfirmed.

Fifth (least likely): The snapshotAgeMinutes computation in the runner or the snapshot's own generatedAt timestamp is incorrect, causing a false staleness reading — however, the evidence shows generatedAtPresent=true and source=github-actions, making a timestamp computation error less probable.
